chapter: Scrapbook: Blue Room acts and the United Fruit ship
title: Blue Room acts: Skyliners, Landry and Verna, Templeton
summary: Riddick identifies acts he worked with at the Blue Room and a Palmer House program from January 1950.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: God bless you, amigo, for your friendship and your kindness during the Orleans State. Two men in North Bay and I went out to California and stayed a couple of nights with when we played there. Now, these are some acts from the blue room that I worked with. The Skyliners. There's a guy.
I have to look at her. Jerry O'Leary.
They were an act. Piano and vocal. Comic. Is he the comic or the pianist? I don't remember. Alec Templeton.

He was a swell fellow. Just as unaffected. Landry and Verna. A dance team. Landry. Landry and Verna. They were from France. January the 6th, 1950. Where were they? I think this was in Chicago. If I'm not mistaken.
Well, you were there at the Palmer House.
Yeah. Yeah. This was a fine bunch of kids. Nice, nice kids. Just sings, singing.
Bill Norvis and the Upstarts. And that's January.
There was a fine, fine dance team. Jacques and Billy C. Jacques and Billy C. They were also from France. Looks like fencing. Yeah. They did the sword dance.
